memory_update.text: PANW should remain a reference anchor, not the main alpha hunt, because the completed CyberArk acquisition validates identity, machine identity, and agentic identity as core AI-era security infrastructure.
TENB is a mid-cap underfollowed candidate for AI/cloud exposure management; verify whether AI Exposure and Tenable One are driving measurable billings, large-customer growth, or net retention.

WK is a non-obvious compliance-control-plane candidate: underfollowed because it sits in reporting/GRC rather than cybersecurity, but AI governance and auditability may make its platform more strategic.

RPD is a speculative small-cap shadow beneficiary in exposure management and AI-native security operations; survival in later layers depends on evidence of growth stabilization and product-led customer expansion.

Layer 1B still needs a separate sweep for public machine-identity, secrets-management, certificate-lifecycle, data-lineage, and industrial cybersecurity vendors because many pure-play assets are private or have been acquired.

node: Cloud cybersecurity and automation infrastructure: identity, machine identity, secrets management, observability, data pipelines, compliance automation, and secure industrial AI workflows
summary: Layer 1B expansion found that the clearest scarce-control-plane chokepoint is identity and exposure management for AI-era cloud environments: human, machine, non-human, and agentic identities; cloud/AI exposure visibility; automated remediation; and regulated reporting/compliance workflows. The reference lane is Palo Alto Networks after closing CyberArk, which confirms that machine and agentic identity security has become a platform battleground. The underfollowed lane points to mid/small-cap software vendors where the market may be less focused on AI copilots and more on mandatory governance, auditability, exposure management, and remediation infrastructure. These are research candidates only, not recommendations.
